sources.title: Superficial and Functional Lymphatic Anatomy of the Upper Extremity.
sources.license: No open reuse license established; publisher copyright applies to article/abstract/images
sources.scope: Retrospective preoperative ICG imaging in breast-cancer patients without clinical/objective lymphedema
supports: Median, radial and ulnar forearm pathways had variable connections to medial/lateral upper-arm pathways.
does_not_support: Mutually exclusive forearm territories from channel names alone
Connection frequency as a flow fraction or hydraulic conductance
Population without cancer or subject-specific canonical anatomy

sources.title: Lower-Limb Lymphatic Drainage Pathways and Lymph Nodes: A CT Lymphangiography Cadaver Study.
sources.license: No open reuse license established; publisher copyright applies to article/abstract/images
sources.scope: 130 lower limbs from 83 fresh cadavers; 19 foot injection sites followed by CT lymphangiography
supports: Four lower-leg pathway groups: anteromedial, anterolateral, posteromedial, posterolateral.
Posterolateral pathways reached popliteal nodes; other groups reached inguinal nodes.
Anteromedial and posteromedial shared destination nodes; anterolateral reached different inguinal nodes.
does_not_support: Four equal-area or equal-volume skin compartments
Distinct node mass ownership for groups sharing a destination

sources.title: Superficial lymphatic system of the upper torso: preliminary radiographic results in human cadavers.
sources.license: No open reuse license established; publisher copyright applies to article/abstract/images
sources.scope: Nine cadavers; upper-torso radiography/dissection with breast cross-sections
supports: Midaxillary line separated anterior and posterior drainage territories in this sample.
Anterior drainage reached external mammary or axillary-vein nodes; posterior drainage reached scapular nodes.
does_not_support: Exact mapping to authored canonical node objects

sources.title: The lymphatic territories of the upper limb: anatomical study and clinical implications.
sources.license: No open reuse license established; publisher copyright applies to article/abstract/images
sources.scope: 14 cadaver upper limbs from 10 cadavers; radiopaque injection and dissection
supports: Most observed upper-limb channels reached one main axillary node; some posterior-forearm channels bypassed it.
No superficial/deep communicating vessels were identified in this study.
does_not_support: Absence of communication in every person or disease state
